revise.statement: Repository is the Flask web framework source (Pallets), dev version 3.2.0.dev at commit 2579ce9f (2025-11-17), ~234 tracked files, src layout, Python >=3.10
Working tree has EVERY tracked file modified vs HEAD with line-ending-only diffs (LF->CRLF); .editorconfig mandates LF; no .gitattributes exists
evidence: git diff ctx.py: only +CRLF lines, content identical

revise.statement: In-flight 3.2 architecture: RequestContext merged into AppContext (single ContextVar _cv_app), deprecated aliases via module __getattr__, dispatch methods now take explicit ctx
3.2 behavior changes: fresh combined context pushed per request/CLI command (no reuse of outer app ctx), fresh g per request, session loaded lazily on first access

Legacy dispatch-signature shim: Flask.__init_subclass__ detects old signatures, wraps subclass overrides with remove_ctx and MUTATES the base Flask class with add_ctx (global, process-wide, can stack-wrap; add_ctx re-reads ctx from the contextvar)
The add_ctx/remove_ctx legacy shim has NO dedicated tests
evidence: grep tests for add_ctx|remove_ctx|old signature: 0 matches

revise.statement: CVE-2026-27205 (missing Vary: Cookie when session accessed without 'accessed' tracking, e.g. membership test) affects this snapshot; fixed upstream in Flask 3.1.3, released after this snapshot

Docs teach obsolete/broken API post-refactor: shell.rst and testing.rst show RequestContext usage and ctx-less preprocess_request()/process_response() calls that raise TypeError in 3.2; api.rst properly marks deprecations
sansio base layer keeps old no-ctx dispatch signatures while concrete Flask overrides add ctx -> interface divergence (relevant for Quart and subclass typing)
evidence: grep sansio/app.py for ctx-taking dispatch methods: none

revise.statement: CI covers py3.10-3.14 including free-threaded 3.13t/3.14t, PyPy, Windows, macOS, min and dev dependency versions
SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS key-ordering fix (CVE-2025-47278 / GHSA-4grg-w6v8-c28g) is present
Deprecated aliases RequestContext/request_ctx are runtime-only (module __getattr__) and invisible to mypy/pyright -> typed extensions fail static checks while runtime works

hypotheses.statement: Upstream Flask 3.2.0.dev mid-flight snapshot. Dominant risks: (a) context-merge compatibility surface with execution gaps — untested legacy dispatch shim that mutates the Flask class and re-reads ctx from contextvars, sansio/Quart interface drift, docs teaching broken calls; (b) CVE-2026-27205 (Vary: Cookie) present, fix released post-snapshot as 3.1.3; (c) CRLF-only dirty working tree is a snapshot-level operational problem. The merge itself is deliberate evolution, not corrosion — risks are execution gaps, not wrong direction.

REVISED (post-challenge): Upstream Flask 3.2.0.dev mid-flight snapshot. The context merge is deliberate evolution (not corrosion): the old two-context model had real ordering/reuse bugs (#5797) and the merge has a planned deprecation path. Findings are therefore execution gaps, not direction errors: (a) legacy dispatch shim untested, mutates Flask class process-wide, re-reads ctx from contextvar — blast radius is every process importing a legacy Flask subclass; (b) CVE-2026-27205 (Vary: Cookie) present — fix landed post-snapshot in 3.1.3; (c) docs teach ctx-less calls that now TypeError (shell.rst/testing.rst); (d) long-tail risks: fresh-g-per-request semantic change and sansio/Quart signature drift; (e) CRLF-only dirty tree is a snapshot-provisioning artifact with operational consequences.
